=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — buyer-side review

The Seller’s update leaves several material risks either unresolved or shifted to Wattlebridge. The “[STANDARD]” labels and reviewer note are the Seller’s characterisation, not evidence that the positions have been agreed or should be accepted. In particular, **do not treat Bluefen consent, Riverlark debt and security, the completion bonuses, or Ironquay IP ownership as resolved**.

This review is based on the Seller’s summary and Disclosure Letter, rather than the full SPA or underlying due-diligence documents. The proposed drafting needs to be checked against those documents and the complete price-adjustment mechanics.

## 1. Liability and remedies: the proposed package is too broad

### General warranty cap, thresholds and time limits

The proposed AUD 4.8 million cap, AUD 25,000 de minimis, AUD 250,000 deductible basket and 18-month notification period significantly restrict recovery. The basket is particularly seller-friendly: once qualifying claims exceed AUD 250,000, the Buyer can recover **only the excess**, not the whole amount. Multiple smaller losses may also fall below the de minimis.

**Push back:** Negotiate a lower threshold and a tipping basket, under which qualifying claims are recoverable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded. Seek a longer general warranty period, including coverage through an audit cycle. Test these provisions against the likely size and timing of Paperbark’s risks rather than accepting the numerical package in isolation.

### Fundamental warranties

Applying the general cap and 18-month period to capacity and title is unacceptable. A defect in ownership or the Seller’s authority can undermine the entire acquisition; an AUD 4.8 million remedy for a AUD 24 million purchase is inadequate.

**Push back:** Give title, ownership, authority and capacity warranties a separate cap up to the purchase price and a substantially longer claim period, subject to applicable law. They should not be subject to the general de minimis or basket.

### Tax, IP and identified risks

The statement that tax and IP are “settled” under the general regime does not adequately address their different risk profiles. Tax liabilities may emerge after 18 months; the Ironquay issue concerns a specifically identified potential defect in valuable IP.

**Push back:** Seek a separate pre-Completion tax covenant or indemnity, with an appropriate period linked to relevant assessment periods, and negotiate appropriate tax warranties. Obtain robust IP ownership and infringement warranties and a specific Ironquay indemnity. Known-risk indemnities should have expressly negotiated caps and periods and should not automatically inherit general warranty thresholds, disclosure or knowledge exclusions.

### All-claims wording and fraud

Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 are said to apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions to **all claims of any nature**. That could undermine negotiated indemnities, price-adjustment rights and other remedies, even if those provisions appear elsewhere in the SPA.

**Push back:** Map each limitation and remedy clause against every claim category and make the agreed exceptions express. Preserve contractual debt and price-adjustment claims, specific indemnities and appropriate equitable relief. Expressly preserve remedies for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation; have NSW counsel check the final non-reliance and exclusive-remedy wording and its interaction with applicable law.

## 2. Disclosure and Buyer knowledge: reject the blanket risk transfer

The letter purports to disclose everything in the data room, accounts, registers and public records. Clause 8.3 goes further, excluding matters actually known **or merely discoverable** by the Buyer or advisers. Together, those provisions could deprive the Buyer of a remedy without the Seller clearly identifying the relevant issue and its implications.

The specific disclosures also identify unresolved facts, not necessarily the legal or financial consequences. For example, the letter expressly does not establish whether the export was accessed or whether the supplier renewals are unavoidable. A blanket disclosure should not turn those uncertainties into accepted Buyer risk.

**Push back:**

- Require disclosure to be **fairly disclosed**, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter against the relevant warranty. Reject disclosure merely because material exists somewhere in the data room or public records.
- Limit any knowledge exclusion to the **actual knowledge of specifically named Buyer individuals** at an agreed time, without imputed adviser knowledge or constructive knowledge from documents or public searches.
- Make clear that disclosure and knowledge do not defeat specifically negotiated indemnities, completion obligations or price adjustments.
- Review each specific disclosure against the underlying documents and proposed warranties. Do not accept the Seller’s general reservation as resolving any required action.

## 3. Completion-critical commercial issues

| Issue | Buyer concern and reasoning | Recommended pushback |
|---|---|---|
| **Bluefen** | Approximately AUD 3.6 million, or 30%, of FY26 revenue is associated with Bluefen. No final written consent or evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied is included. Treating delivery of a written consent alone as satisfaction could leave the Buyer exposed to a conditional or ineffective consent. | Make Completion conditional on receipt of a valid written consent **and satisfaction or effective waiver of all associated conditions**, on terms acceptable to the Buyer and without adverse changes. Require evidence and an appropriate long-stop/termination mechanism. Review DD-002 and the actual consent. |
| **Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding and no final security discharge is included. A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer bearing debt and security risk contrary to the debt-free/cash-free baseline. | Require a binding payout statement and irrevocable discharge/release arrangements effective **at Completion**, with completion funds paid directly as required and evidence of release and necessary registrations. Ensure the debt is deducted from the Seller’s proceeds or otherwise dealt with under the agreed debt-free mechanism, without double counting. Review all secured obligations, change-control requirements and discharge documents. |
| **Completion bonuses** | DD-005 records AUD 420,000 of conditional bonuses omitted from the funds flow; possible payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unquantified. They are not established as presently payable regardless of Completion and employment conditions, but may become a Company cost on Completion. | Determine who is liable, when the conditions are satisfied and the on-costs. Specify Seller funding or an appropriate debt-like/price adjustment, and show the payment and funding route in the funds flow. Prevent double counting in completion accounts or other adjustments. |
| **Ironquay IP** | Transfer of SOW3 materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. The AUD 180,000 open item is evidence requiring investigation, not independent proof of non-payment; there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the room. The existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment may not cover loss from a failure of ownership. | Verify the payment position and obtain evidence of cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment or other effective vesting document by Completion. Expand the specific indemnity to cover losses and costs arising from the ownership/transfer defect, not merely payment of the fee, with bespoke limitations. Assess whether the materials are material to the business. |
| **Export/privacy incident** | A link was sent to an unintended external address; approximately 1,240 records may be involved. Access, scope, notification obligations and loss remain unknown. It is premature both to dismiss the incident and to call it a confirmed breach. | Require the investigation, access-log preservation and assessment of affected data and notification obligations to be progressed promptly by appropriately qualified advisers. Obtain status and remediation information before signing/Completion; consider a tailored indemnity or other protection once facts are better known, including investigation, remediation and legally required notification costs. Do not delay any notification that applicable law requires. |

## 4. Other diligence and drafting points

- **Sandbar renewals — AUD 330,000:** DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together. The present record does not establish whether the three AUD 110,000 costs are accrued, unavoidable, terminable or ordinary-course. Determine timing, contractual commitments and accounting treatment. Include any appropriate liability or debt-like adjustment under the agreed mechanism, avoiding double recovery; do not automatically deduct the full amount.
- **Office lease:** DD-007 identifies a notification obligation, not a share-sale consent requirement. Confirm timing and responsibility for the notice and obtain evidence it is given when due. Do not invent a consent condition without contractual support.
- **Mossvale:** DD-009 restricts assignment but does not itself say that a share sale requires consent. Check the full agreement for change-of-control and related provisions and whether any assignment is contemplated; do not assume consent is required solely from the stated restriction.
- **Share title:** The register supports the stated 100% holding but is not a complete verification of title or absence of encumbrances. Check the register and corporate records, issued share capital and any options or rights, and obtain completion deliverables and fundamental warranties covering ownership, authority, full title and freedom from security interests.
- **Price mechanics:** Review the full definition of debt, cash and any working-capital adjustment, the calculation date and dispute process. Ensure the AUD 24 million baseline is implemented consistently in the funds flow and completion accounts, especially for Riverlark, bonuses and any qualifying supplier liabilities. Identify who bears transaction expenses and avoid gaps or double counting.

## Recommended negotiating priorities

1. **Make Bluefen and Riverlark completion protections effective:** do not complete on an unverified or conditional Bluefen consent, or with Riverlark repayment and security release left for later.
2. **Rebuild the liability architecture:** separate fundamental, tax and identified-risk protection from general warranty limits; preserve fraud and other expressly negotiated remedies.
3. **Reject blanket disclosure and constructive knowledge:** require fair, sufficiently detailed disclosure and narrow any Buyer knowledge exclusion.
4. **Resolve the money and ownership issues before Completion:** verify Ironquay payment and secure IP vesting; determine and fund the bonuses and on-costs; reconcile all items with the debt-free/cash-free mechanics.
5. **Investigate the export and supplier renewals on evidence:** reserve proportionate protection without treating uncertain liabilities as either confirmed or immaterial.
